title: Fppf descent and base change of finite algebraic-space morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Call $f$ finite if every scheme base change $X\times_YT\to T$ is represented by a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $\{Y_i\to Y\}_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed jointly surjective family of flat locally finitely presented algebraic-space morphisms, with these properties tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Then $f$ is finite if and only if every $X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 0426 (lemma-descending-property-finite), fppf specialization of fpqc locality; finite on scheme tests is the finite case of spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03ZQ (lemma-integral-local).

proof.text: Finiteness in the stated scheme-test sense is preserved by every algebraic-space base change: for $Y\prime\to Y$ and a scheme $T\to Y\prime$, the test pullback $(X\times_Y Y\prime)\times_{Y\prime}T$ is $X\times_YT$, with the same projection to $T$, by the fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. If $f$ is finite, this projection is a finite scheme morphism by hypothesis. This proves the forward implication and fixes the base-change identifications used below.

source.place: Tag 03ZQ (lemma-integral-local), representable finite condition; base-change identification

proof.text: Assume each $f_i:X\times_Y Y_i\to Y_i$ is finite. Each $f_i$ is affine: on an affine scheme test its source is a scheme finite over that affine scheme, hence affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](2). Apply the affine clause of [lem-sfb-space-four-property-fppf-descent] to the given covering. Thus $f$ is affine in that node's sense: $X\times_YU$ is an affine scheme for every affine scheme $U\to Y$. Now let $T\to Y$ be any scheme and $X_T=X\times_YT$, an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For an affine open $U\subseteq T$, $X_U=X_T\times_TU=X\times_YU$ is an affine scheme, and it is an open subspace of $X_T$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace]: for a scheme $W\to X_T$, $W\times_{X_T}X_U=W\times_TU$ is the open preimage of $U$ in $W$. By [lem-sfb-space-largest-schematic-open] each $X_U$ lies in the schematic open subspace $A\subseteq X_T$. For every scheme $W\to X_T$ the open subscheme $W\times_{X_T}A$ contains every $W\times_TU$, and these cover $W$ as $U$ runs through an affine open cover of $T$; so $W\times_{X_T}A=W$, every $W\to X_T$ factors through $A$, and $X_T=A$ is a scheme. Its preimage over each affine open $U$ is the affine scheme $X_U$, so $f_T:X_T\to T$ is an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. This establishes representability before applying any scheme descent theorem.

Fix an affine scheme $T\to Y$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-fppf-finite-affine-refinement] to obtain affine schemes $V_j$, a finite set $J$, maps $V_j\to Y_{a(j)}$ over $Y$, and a flat surjective map $p:T\prime=\coprod_{j\in J}V_j\to T$ with $T\prime$ affine. The equality of the two composites $V_j\to Y$ identifies $X_T\times_TV_j$ with $(X\times_Y Y_{a(j)})\times_{Y_{a(j)}}V_j$, so its projection to $V_j$ is finite by the assumed scheme tests of $f_{a(j)}$. This identification is the one induced by the projections, using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

The coprojections $V_j\to T\prime$ are open immersions and their images cover $T\prime$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The restriction of the scheme morphism $f_{T\prime}:X_T\times_TT\prime\to T\prime$ to this open $V_j$ is the finite morphism of Step 3: both pullbacks have the same projection characterization. The open-cover equivalence (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] therefore shows that $f_{T\prime}$ is finite. If $J$ is empty, $T\prime$ is empty, its pullback source is empty, and the same empty-open-cover criterion still applies.

source.place: Tag 01WI (lemma-finite-local), open-cover criterion; schemes.tex Tags 01JB, 01JC for the coproduct opens

proof.text: The morphism $p:T\prime\to T$ is a morphism between affine schemes, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3). It is flat and surjective by Step 3. Both $X_T$ and $X_T\times_TT\prime$ are schemes by Step 2. Apply [lem-sbc-finite-morphism-fpqc-descent] to $f_T$ and $p$, with Step 4 supplying finiteness after pullback. It follows that $f_T$ is finite. This proves finiteness on every affine scheme test, with no quasi-compactness imposed on $Y$ or on the original covering members.

source.place: Tag 02LA (lemma-descending-property-finite), applied after affine representability descent

proof.text: Finally let $T\to Y$ be any scheme test. Step 2 makes $f_T$ an affine morphism of schemes. Cover $T$ by its affine opens $U$. Its restriction to $U$ is canonically $f_U$ and is finite by Step 5. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target](3) to conclude that $f_T$ is finite. Thus every scheme test has the required finite scheme source and projection, proving the converse. For $T=\varnothing$ the empty cover proves the same statement; if the original family is empty, joint surjectivity forces the target to be empty, as also allowed by the refinement statement.
